hero.oneLiner: An integrated iron and steel manufacturing company specializing in customized engineering solutions, which according to CRISIL is one of India's largest metal rolls producers, meeting 10.00-11.5% of the country's demand in Fiscal 2026.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: An integrated iron and steel manufacturing company specializing in customized engineering solutions, which according to CRISIL is one of India's largest metal rolls producers, meeting 10.00-11.5% of the country's demand in Fiscal 2026.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Behari Lal Engineering manufactures precision engineered components for critical industrial applications - metal rolls for rolling mills, engineering castings (500 kg to 20 MT per unit), carbon/alloy/stainless steel bars (6 mm to 230 mm), and forging ingots and forged shafts/blocks (500 kg to 15 tons). It operates 2 integrated divisions in Mandi Gobindgarh, Punjab - a Steel Melting Shop (SMS) and Foundry Division and a Rolling Mill Division - with a digital melting shop, ladle refining furnace, vacuum degassing, foundry, heat treatment, machine shops and rolling mills. Products are supplied to 1,825 customers as of March 31, 2026 across automobile, steel, mining, infrastructure and construction, power, aerospace and defence and cement industries in India and, since April 1, 2024, exported to 21 countries across 5 continents.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- BLC Metals Private Limited — Group Company: The Company's only Group Company; engaged in business activities similar to those of the Company (common pursuits / conflict-of-interest risk flagged). Rajesh Garg and Dinesh Garg are also directors of BLC Metals. Not listed; not party to any pending litigation with a material impact on the Company.
- Belco Special Steels Private Limited (BSSPL) — Amalgamated into the Company: Merged with the Company through a scheme of amalgamation; its business is now the Company's Rolling Mill Division.
- Parkash Multimetals Private Limited (PMPL) — Amalgamated into the Company: Merged with the Company through a scheme of amalgamation; its operations are part of the Company's SMS and Foundry Division. Following the amalgamation the entity was rebranded as Behari Lal Engineering Limited (BLEL).
- SG Tech Engineering Private Limited — Investor Selling Shareholder: Offering up to 2,732,755 Equity Shares in the Offer for Sale; residual holding 1,171,180 Equity Shares.
- Yogita Garg — Promoter Group Selling Shareholder: Offering up to 2,143,623 Equity Shares; residual holding 1,215,977 Equity Shares.
- Dinesh Kumar Garg HUF — Promoter Group Selling Shareholder: Offering up to 150,000 Equity Shares; residual holding 2,817,125 Equity Shares.
- No holding company, subsidiary, joint venture or associate — Structure confirmation: As on the date of the Red Herring Prospectus the Company has no holding company, no subsidiary and no joint ventures or associate companies.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Metal Rolls:** Alloy cast steel rolls, Alloy steel base adamite rolls, Graphitic steel rolls, S.G. Iron Pearlitic Rolls, S.G. Iron Bainitic/Accicular Rolls, Alloyed indefinite chill rolls, Forged rolls
- **Engineering Castings:** Special-grade engineering castings, per unit weight 500 kg to 20 MT, for steel, iron, mining and aggregate crushers, power and sugar industries
- **Alloy Steel Products:** Carbon, alloy steel and stainless steel bars in rounds, round corner square, flats and hex, 6 mm to 230 mm, Tool steel (recently introduced), Valve steel (recently introduced)
- **Forging Ingots and Forged Shafts / Blocks:** Forging ingots in round, square, rectangular and custom shapes, 500 kg to 15 tons, in carbon steels, alloy steels, stainless steels and special tool steels, Forged shafts / blocks
- **Others:** Job work, High sea sales, traded goods and sale of by-products

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Backward and forward integration within a single site cluster: the Company describes itself as an integrated iron and steel manufacturing company operating two integrated divisions - a Steel Melting Shop (SMS) and Foundry Division and a Rolling Mill Division. The SMS runs 12 MT fully digital medium-frequency induction furnaces in twin-shell configuration with secondary metallurgy via ladle refining furnace (LRF) and vacuum degassing (VD); the foundry has an in-house engineering and pattern development unit, continuous sand mixers, mechanised fettling via automatic shakeout, a sand reclamation plant, shot blasting and automatic paint booths; downstream are heat treatment furnaces, machine shops (>100,000 sq ft covered, CNC lathes, boring machines, roll grinding, VTL/CNC VTL, plano and CNC vertical milling) and rolling mills. Manufacturing and machining processes are described as overlapping and fungible, so the available (installed) capacity of the SMS and Foundry Division can vary with the product mix being run. Upstream, raw material (scrap, ingots, ferro alloys) is procured directly from domestic manufacturers and international suppliers without middlemen, on purchase orders rather than long term contracts; internally generated scrap is re-melted and recycled. Downstream, the Company sells directly through its in-house sales team, keeping middle-men and agents out of the sales process because products are highly customised and engineered; orders are purchase-order based with customer projections used for production planning, and long term contracts are generally avoided due to steel price volatility. Utilities: a 66 KvA sub-station, grid power from the Punjab State Electricity Board, ground water, and around 2 MW of installed rooftop solar. Corporate structure was consolidated through a Scheme of Amalgamation (NCLT Chandigarh order dated August 22, 2024) merging Belco Special Steels Private Limited (now the Rolling Mill Division) and Parkash Multimetals Private Limited (now part of the SMS and Foundry Division) into the Company.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Retaining existing customers and augmenting the customer base - repeat customers were 84.69% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2026 and several key customers have relationships of over 10 years; there are no long-term contracts, business runs on purchase orders
- Robust overlapping and fungible manufacturing processes that enable high capacity utilisation - because SMS and Foundry Division processes are fungible, available (installed) capacity varies with the product mix chosen in a period; total utilisation was 87.71% in Fiscal 2026
- Managing operating expenses - cost of materials consumed is the most significant expense at Rs 2,806.58 million, Rs 2,716.46 million and Rs 2,745.21 million (61.02%, 60.78% and 68.62% of total expenses) in Fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024; manufacturing expenses and employee benefits expense are the other important elements
- Power and fuel cost intensity - cost of power and fuel was Rs 351.46 million (7.64% of total expenses) in Fiscal 2026 versus Rs 326.98 million (7.32%) in Fiscal 2025 and Rs 236.82 million (5.92%) in Fiscal 2024, and is expected to rise with installed capacity, driving the solar investment
- Product mix shift toward high value products (engineering castings, metal rolls, valve/die/tool steel), which the Company expects to improve operating profit margin - EBITDA margin moved from 13.67% (FY24) to 16.01% (FY25) to 18.97% (FY26) and EBITDA per ton from Rs 7,433.60 to Rs 9,125.51 to Rs 11,494.66
- Working capital cycle - net working capital rose to Rs 1,924.50 million (132 working capital days) as at March 31, 2026 from Rs 1,453.68 million (104 days) and Rs 1,196.40 million (98 days); cash conversion cycle was 93, 72 and 89 days as inventory days rose from 34 to 42 to 57
- General demand for steel - according to CRISIL domestic steel demand logged an 11.6% CAGR between Fiscals 2020 and 2026 and is expected to accelerate at a CAGR of approximately 6.5-8.5% to 225-250 MT by Fiscal 2031

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Augment installed capacity in line with expected business growth, including expanding foundry operations, roll making capacity and related machine shops, and setting up the third (Upcoming) Manufacturing Facility at Village Salani
- Optimise the product portfolio to cater more to higher value and value-added products - engineering castings, metal rolls and alloy steel grades such as valve steel, die steel and tool steel; high value products were 57.78% of revenue in Fiscal 2026 versus 45.45% in Fiscal 2025 and 44.65% in Fiscal 2024
- Upgrade melting and machining capacity and install an open die forging press to internalise forging and stop outsourcing, improving product mix and operating margins
- Broaden the end-user industry base and export market by capitalising on growth in the metal rolls and engineering casting industry, targeting new end-uses such as automobile OEM, plastic moulding, oil and gas, chemical processing and the forging industry, and capitalising on the China+1 strategy
- Bid for higher value tenders from select customers including some of India's largest steel manufacturers and large public sector undertakings including entities in the defence sector
- Increase wallet share with existing customers by introducing new products and grades - ICDP rolls, HSS rolls and High Temperature/Creep Resistant Grade Steels for injection moulding, defence and aerospace and cutting industries
- Rationalise power cost through rooftop solar panels and a new grounded captive solar power plant under the PSERC (Harnessing of Captive Power Generation) Regulations, 2022

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company operates 2 facilities in Mandi Gobindgarh, Punjab with a combined installed capacity of 119,690 MT (Manufacturing Facility 1 at Village Salani, the SMS and Foundry Division, 54,690 MT; Manufacturing Facility 2 at Village Turan, the Rolling Mill Division, 65,000 MT) and has recently commenced construction of a third, Upcoming Manufacturing Facility at Village Salani, Tehsil Amloh, District Fatehgarh Sahib, on approximately 2.07 acres out of 6.47 acres of recently purchased land. Net Proceeds of the Fresh Issue are earmarked for new equipment and machinery with civil work at both existing facilities plus rooftop solar panels at each. As certified by GATS India Ltd (Independent Chartered Engineer, certificate dated August 6, 2026), the new machinery will raise Manufacturing Facility 2 installed capacity by 15,000 MT from 65,000 MT, while Manufacturing Facility 1 sees no net change - metal rolls and engineering castings capacity rises by 5,000 MT but ingots capacity falls by 5,000 MT. Rooftop solar generating capacity rises by 1,000 kWp at each facility (from 1,362 kWp at MF1 and 500 kWp at MF2). Separately, the Company is establishing additional capacity for engineering castings, metal rolls and ingots by upgrading the Casting Shop, Moulding Shop and Machine Shop with advanced CNC and VTL machines and additional heat treatment furnaces, and plans a 1600T hydraulic open die forging press and a 2 MT open die forging hammer (with 7 MT and 5 MT manipulators) to establish forged products installed capacity of 15,000 MT annually and eliminate outsourced forging. A grounded captive solar power plant application under the PSERC Regulations dated May 25, 2026 is pending.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Long standing relationships with a large number of customers across a wide array of end-user industries with stringent qualification processes - revenue from repeat customers was Rs 4,522.77 million, Rs 4,372.98 million and Rs 3,570.50 million (84.69%, 86.10% and 80.04% of revenue from operations) in Fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024; top 10 customers for Fiscal 2026 have been with the Company for an average of 6 years; 1,825 customers catered to as of March 31, 2026
- Diversified product portfolio catering to varied application industries - top 3 segments (Alloy Steel Products, Metal Rolls, Engineering Castings) contributed Rs 2,446.10 million, Rs 1,407.41 million and Rs 1,043.39 million (45.81%, 26.35% and 19.54%) of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2026
- Strategically located Manufacturing Facilities with advanced equipment and robust overlapping, fungible processes enabling high capacity utilisation - 2 facilities across approximately 790,000 sq ft with combined installed capacity of 119,690 MT; total capacity utilisation of 87.71%, 90.30% and 85.47% in Fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024
- Locational advantage in Mandi Gobindgarh, one of India's oldest steel hubs - NH-44 and SH-12A connectivity, 2 dry ports around 40 km, Chandigarh International Airport 60 km, access to the Amritsar-Kolkata Industrial Corridor, and direct sourcing of raw material from domestic manufacturers and international suppliers without middlemen
- Robust presence leveraging the legacy and experience of the Promoters and domain expertise of the management team - over 2 decades in the steel industry, founder-Chairman a director for 30 years; workforce of 667 trained employees and 359 persons on contract as on May 31, 2026
- Track record of financial performance and consistent growth - revenue from operations grew at a CAGR of 9.41% and profit after tax at a CAGR of 34.38% between Fiscal 2024 and Fiscal 2026 (as stated by the Company)
- Qualified supplier status with global OEMs requiring facility assessments, process audits and part testing before purchase orders are awarded; according to CRISIL these long-standing approvals create high entry barriers
- Sustainability positioning - approximately 2 MW of installed rooftop solar, use of 100% recycled steel scrap, direct raw material sourcing and 4 acres of dedicated green belt

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Customer concentration without long-term contracts — Revenue from the top 10 customers was Rs 2,029.21 million, Rs 2,027.16 million and Rs 1,686.51 million (38.00%, 39.91% and 37.81% of revenue from operations) in Fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024, with the largest single customer at 6.96% in Fiscal 2026. The Company does not enter into long term contracts and its business is based on purchase orders, so demand can fall away at short notice.
- Raw material cost pass-through and supplier dependence — Cost of material consumed - primarily scrap and ferro alloys sourced domestically and internationally - was 61.02%, 60.78% and 68.62% of total expenses in Fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024. There are no long-term supply agreements with third party suppliers, and steel pricing is subject to market demand, volatility and economic conditions.
- Working capital intensity — Net working capital was Rs 1,924.50 million as at March 31, 2026 (132 working capital days) versus Rs 1,453.68 million (104 days) at March 31, 2025 and Rs 1,196.40 million (98 days) at March 31, 2024, with inventory days rising from 34 to 42 to 57. Sanctioned working capital facilities were Rs 691.03 million as on May 31, 2026 with Rs 94.36 million outstanding.
- Product concentration — Alloy steel products, metal rolls and engineering castings cumulatively contributed more than 90.00% of revenue from operations in each of Fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024 (91.70%, 93.14% and 94.29% from sale of customised products), so a downturn in any one of these segments is material.
- Single-location manufacturing — All manufacturing operations - and the Upcoming Manufacturing Facility - are located in Mandi Gobindgarh, Punjab, exposing the Company to concentrated regional, regulatory, labour and natural-event risk.
- Geographic revenue concentration in India — Sales to customers in India were Rs 4,860.47 million, Rs 4,859.33 million and Rs 4,245.17 million (91.02%, 95.67% and 95.17% of revenue from operations) in Fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024. Domestic sub-total was essentially flat between Fiscal 2025 and Fiscal 2026; growth came from exports.
- Execution and capex risk on the third facility and unplaced orders — Construction of the Upcoming Manufacturing Facility has only recently commenced and its completion and operation are contingent on obtaining various approvals; delays could cause cost and time overruns. The Company has not yet placed orders for the capital expenditure equipment and machinery to be funded from the Net Proceeds, and the fund requirements have not been appraised by any bank or financial institution.
- Order book is not a guarantee of future revenue — The Order Book was Rs 1,182.87 million as on March 31, 2026 (Rs 930.03 million and Rs 855.45 million at the two prior year ends) and Rs 1,785.69 million as of May 31, 2026, but the Company states that current order book value is not necessarily indicative of future growth and some orders may be modified or cancelled.
- Promoter and related-party dependence, and conflict of interest with the Group Company — The Company has entered into related party transactions (salaries and remuneration, rent, loans) and has availed unsecured loans including from related parties which are repayable on demand. Group Company BLC Metals Private Limited is engaged in similar business activities, creating a potential conflict of interest, and Promoters will continue to exercise significant control after the Offer.
